patch.summary:
Choose Tidio only if your buying job matches “Live chat and AI messaging — Starter $24.17/mo annual (100 billable convos); Growth from $” rather than Zendesk Suite's shape. Choose Zendesk Suite only if your buying job matches “Enterprise helpdesk and Suite omnichannel — Support Team from $19/agent/mo annual; Suite T” rather than Tidio's shape. Workflow advantage: Tidio leans live-chat-support; Zendesk Suite leans helpdesk-ticketing, omnichannel-support. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Tidio is Live chat and AI messaging — Starter $24.17/mo annual (100 billable convos); Growth from $49.17. Primary live-chat; CS secondary.; Zendesk Suite is Enterprise helpdesk and Suite omnichannel — Support Team from $19/agent/mo annual; Suite Team $55, Suite Pro $115..
- Company-size focus: Tidio (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Zendesk Suite (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Tidio-leaning live-chat-support vs Zendesk Suite-leaning helpdesk-ticketing, omnichannel-support.
- Researched limits: Tidio — Conversation-cap pricing — high traffic sites need Growth+ tiers; Zendesk Suite — Suite Pro at $115/agent/mo annual is expensive for SMB teams.

Limitations — Tidio: Conversation-cap pricing — high traffic sites need Growth+ tiers; Not a full helpdesk/ITSM — thin ticketing vs Freshdesk; Zendesk Suite: Suite Pro at $115/agent/mo annual is expensive for SMB teams; Zendesk Sell (CRM) is a separate product — do not conflate slugs.

Poor-fit cases: Tidio is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Conversation-cap pricing — high traffic sites need Growth+ tiers · Zendesk Suite is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Suite Pro at $115/agent/mo annual is expensive for SMB teams · Avoid Tidio if you actually need Zendesk Suite's motion (Enterprise helpdesk and Suite omnichannel — Support Team from $19/agent/mo annua)
